context: Treat this as a release-blocking ADR. The chosen v1 is completion-oriented: no background heartbeat, no plan mutation tool, and no model-triggered execution of stored verification commands. Structural planning failures return exact human remediation and release the streamlined claim; code/verification/scope failures retain it.
description: Write the binding ADR for the streamlined agent surface before schema or adapter work: stable principal versus session attribution, same-principal adoption and audited cross-principal takeover, one live claim per agent workflow, verification execution policy, structural-gate release policy, Git baseline divergence handling, advisory-not-authenticated claim language, no v1 heartbeat, and local versus hosted support labels.

anti_patterns.instead: call it claim-coordinated and document advisory ownership
anti_patterns.why: --actor is spoofable and database credentials are the real boundary

anti_patterns.dont: Leave a gate with no reachable remediation
anti_patterns.instead: map it to an action or a terminal exact human command and release policy
anti_patterns.why: the model would loop while renewing a claim

anti_patterns.instead: use a stable principal and record session separately
anti_patterns.why: routine restart or fork would lock work for the full TTL

preserves.behavior: Claims remain cooperative coordination, never an authentication boundary
No implementation item starts until this ADR resolves every named decision
The Pi model tool never gains verification overrides, restore, migration, or destructive administration
